newsitem.title: UK: OFWAT's Byatt says no new resource development yet.
newsitem.headline: OFWAT's Byatt says no new resource development yet.

text.p: UK water industry regulator OFWAT head Ian Byatt said on Monday that no new resource developments would be allowed until he is satisfied that leakage is at economic levels and that demand is being properly managed.
"A policy of balanced leakage reduction and demand management defers the need to invest in expensive additional water resources," Byatt told the water summit.
The emergency conference has been called to tackle leakage and the country's worst drought in 200 years.

Thames Water Plc is reported to be drawing up plans for a new 800 million stg reservoir. OFWAT figures show that Thames is losing 38 percent of the treated water it puts into the mains, more than any other company.
Byatt said longer-term demand and supply issues would be "an important element" in his 1999 price review. He expected to be able to cut prices in real terms at the 1999 review.
He added that companies should adopt "a total cost approach with a minimum cost solution -- one pound on conservation should balance with one pound on resources".
